criteria.text: Hyperglycemia secondary to hypercortisolism in adults with endogenous Cushing's syndrome who have type 2 diabetes mellitus or glucose intolerance and have failed surgery or are not candidates for surgery (Indications and Usage).
Patient is an adult, 18 years of age or older (Indications and Usage).
Diagnosis of type 2 diabetes mellitus or glucose intolerance (approval criterion 2).
Has failed surgery or is not a candidate for surgery (approval criterion 3).

notes: Partial encoding from Alaska Medicaid Korlym (mifepristone) criteria Version 1. Last updated 12/11/2012; Approved 01/18/2013. No explicit effective date is printed; effective_date uses the approval date 2013-01-18.

Encoded: closed endogenous Cushing's hyperglycemia indication, adult age from the indication, diagnosis of Cushing's syndrome, type 2 diabetes mellitus or glucose intolerance, and failed surgery or not a surgery candidate. Diagnosis and surgery history require documentation verification.
Limitations of Use: Do not use for the treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus unrelated to endogenous Cushing's syndrome.
Duration (notes only): initial authorization may be approved for 3 months. Reauthorization with documentation of clinical improvement may be approved for 9 months.
Dispensing limit (notes only): 30-day supply with maximum 1200 mg once daily, not to exceed 20 mg/kg/day. Available as a 300 mg tablet. Numeric quantity enforcement is not encoded.
Documentation verification, duration, reauthorization and dispensing limits require manual review; this pack remains partial. Alternatives require independent evaluation of their own criteria.
